finding: Two-reference local FLUX generation can preserve identity and watercolor treatment for neutral full-body views without a structure-control image. The approved profile-left uses only the approved front character master and one approved style reference; its side pose is constrained by the prompt and human review. Prompt-only 45-degree views still failed face/body alignment. Approved-view-anchor interpolation also failed: the left result collapsed to near-profile and the right result separated face gaze from rearward, duplicated legs. Existing 8 GB OpenPose plus IP-Adapter and Ctrl-X experiments separately showed only partial structure or identity retention. A further Ctrl-X preflight with a landmark-plus-blockout 3D projection and the approved front appearance completed in 18.27 seconds at 1.45 GiB reserved VRAM, but rendered object-like artifacts instead of the character; it failed identity, full body, and three-quarter yaw. The abstract blockout is therefore not a usable Ctrl-X structure input. A ControlNet++ OpenPose+depth preflight with the official union SDXL checkpoint and Pose Depot guide also did not reach image generation on this 7.53 GiB GPU: sequential offload left custom transformer tensors on meta device, while model offload OOMed during SDXL UNet loading. Zero123++ v1.1 was then tested only as a fixed-view geometry proposal from the approved front image. It produced the six-view grid on the local GPU, but the side and three-quarter cells were cut by canvas boundaries, lost the head, or collapsed the body silhouette. It therefore cannot provide a usable human turnaround structure proposal and its candidate grid was removed. In contrast, a standard SD 1.5 depth ControlNet with a temporary human 3D depth guide passed the anatomy-and-occlusion gate at 512x768: one head, torso, pelvis, two legs, and two feet remained in a coherent high-angle three-quarter arrangement. Adding a single approved front reference through the compatible SD 1.5 IP-Adapter retained broad teal hair and watercolor-like line cues at scales 0.65 and 0.90, but did not preserve Mira's white jacket, navy flap bag, or one diagonal strap. This branch therefore fails the appearance contract and does not validate FLUX conditioning. A separate detector-derived eight-direction OpenPose/skeleton attempt was rejected before image conditioning: synthetic rear and profile drafts yielded missing heads, disconnected joints, and false background keypoints. OpenPose body skeletons do not provide a reliable eight-direction turnaround input in this pipeline.
decision: Use only the approved four-direction full-body baseline: front, profile-left, rear, and profile-right. The rear three-quarter images were removed rather than retained as supplementary references. This set is a character reference baseline, not an eight-direction turnaround and not proof of untested three-quarter camera yaw.
next_required_method: Do not resume the eight-direction branch or use mirrored images as additional coverage. The Canny/OpenPose dynamic-pose experiment was removed and is not turnaround evidence. Any future camera-yaw expansion requires a newly reviewed target-specific structure method.
